content: Elevations in hepatic enzymes have been observed. Patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions to mirikizumab or any of its excipients should not use this medication. Currently, data from case reports on the use of mirikizumab in pregnant women are insufficient to determine the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. However, monoclonal antibodies, including mirikizumab, can be actively transported across the placenta and may cause immunosuppression in infants exposed in utero. There is no available data on the presence of mirikizumab in human breast milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. Mirikizumab is generally considered acceptable for use, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. When preparing the medication for administration, a 9% NaCl or D5W solution may be used, and the time required to flush the IV line is in addition to the minimum 30-minute infusion time. For subcutaneous injections, the recommended sites include the abdomen, thigh, and back of the upper arm. It is important to rotate injection sites and avoid areas where the skin is tender, bruised, erythematous, or indurated. The product does not contain preservatives, so any unused portion must be discarded. It should not be reused. The vial and prefilled pen are not made with dry natural rubber latex. The product must not be frozen, and it should not be used if it has been frozen. Additionally, the medication should not be shaken and must be stored in its original carton to protect it from light until the time of use. The product is sterile and preservative-free, and any unused portion should be discarded.
